nodes.name: Solvothermal synthesis Pd₁Fe SAA@PC
nodes.procedure: DPPF (0.36 mmol, 200 mg) was dissolved by ultrasound in toluene solution (10 mL) for 10 min and then mixed with palladium(II) acetylacetonate (0.027 mmol, 3 mg). After vigorous stirring for 10 min at ambient temperature, the mixture was transferred into a 25 mL Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave and heated at 230 °C for 3 h. The white product was collected via centrifugation and further washed with deionized water and ethanol two times, respectively. After vacuum freeze-drying, Pd₁Fe SAA@PC were obtained.

nodes.name: Pyrolysis synthesis Pd1Fe SAA
nodes.procedure: 1 g of DCDA and 0.1 g of trimesic acid were dissolved in 20 mL of ethanol, while 2 mg of Pd(acac)₂ and 10 mg of Fe(NO₃)₂·9H₂O were also added to the solution. Then, the mixed solution was placed in a rotary evaporator at 50 °C, adjusted to the appropriate speed, and stopped when the solvent evaporates. Subsequently, the dried product was ground into powder and placed in a porcelain boat in a tube furnace. To prepare the Pd₁Fe SAA, the boat (containing the precursor materials) was annealed at 800 °C under a N₂ atmosphere for 2 h. The ramping rate used was 5 °C per minute. After annealing, the boat was allowed to cool to room temperature naturally. Following the annealing process, the prepared Pd₁Fe SAA was thoroughly washed with ethanol and deionized water to remove any impurities or residues. Finally, the samples were dried in a vacuum at 60 °C overnight to ensure the complete removal of any remaining solvents.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS shows uniform distribution of Pd, Fe, P, and C elements in Pd₁Fe SAA@PC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) corresponding to TEM images showed a uniform distribution of Pd, Fe, P, and C in Pd₁Fe SAA@PC (Figure 1c).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows carbon layer encapsulating Pd₁Fe alloy ('armor' structure) with average lattice spacing of 2.06 Å (+1.2% tensile strain vs Fe(101)).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image revealed that the outer layer of the Pd₁Fe alloy was enveloped by a carbon layer... The average lattice spacing of Pd₁Fe in Pd₁Fe SAA@PC across the 10 layers is 2.06 Å.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM shows uniform distribution of brighter Pd atoms and darker Fe atoms in Pd₁Fe SAA@PC spheres with alternating atomic distribution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-magnification high-angle annular dark-field scanning TEM (HAADF-STEM) images clearly depicted the uniform distribution of Pd and Fe atoms in the Pd₁Fe SAA@PC spheres (Figure 1e,f).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows peak at 2θ = 44° corresponding to α-Fe (110) diffraction shifted to lower angles for Pd₁Fe SAA@PC, indicating partial lattice stretching.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns of Pd₁Fe SAA@PC, Pd₁Fe SAA@C, and Fe NP@PC exhibited a peak at 2θ = 44°, corresponding to the (110) diffractions of α-Fe... The peak was observed to shift to lower angles for Pd₁Fe SAA@PC.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows high graphitic carbon content in Pd₁Fe SAA@PC with I_D/I_G ratio of 0.76.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman spectra demonstrated that Pd₁Fe SAA@PC had a high level of graphitic carbon, as evidenced by a relative I_D/I_G ratio of 0.76.

nodes.characterization_summary: N2 adsorption-desorption reveals well-distributed pore structure of 1.688 nm in carbon shell surface of Pd₁Fe SAA@PC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The N2 adsorption-desorption isotherms (Figure S8) revealed that the carbon shell surface of Pd₁Fe SAA@PC had a well-distributed pore structure (1.688 nm).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS confirms Pd and Fe content matching SAA and nanoparticle characteristics (Table S1).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The results of inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry showed that the content of Pd and Fe matched the characteristics of the SAA and nanoparticles (Table S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: C K-edge XANES shows peaks at 285.5 eV (π*C=C), 288.5 eV (π*C-P), and 292.5 eV (σ*C-C), confirming C-P bond presence.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The C K-edge spectrum of Pd₁Fe SAA@PC (Figure 2a) exhibited three distinct peaks located at 285.5 eV (peak a), 288.5 eV (peak b), and 292.5 eV (peak c).

nodes.characterization_summary: Pd K-edge absorption threshold between PdO and Pd foil indicates Pd oxidation state between +2 and 0 in Pd₁Fe SAA@PC catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2b displays the edge position of Pd₁Fe SAA@PC between PdO and Pd foil, indicating that the average oxidation state of Pd was between that in the two reference samples.

nodes.characterization_summary: FT Pd K-edge EXAFS shows peaks at 1.47 Å (Pd-C), 1.90 Å (Pd-P), 2.42 Å (Pd-Fe); no Pd-Pd bond confirms atomic dispersion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fourier transform (FT) Pd K-edge EXAFS spectra of Pd₁Fe SAA@PC displayed three obvious FT peaks at 1.47, 1.90, and 2.42 Å mainly attributed to the scattering of Pd-C, Pd-P, and Pd-Fe coordination.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe K-edge position between Fe⁰ and Fe²⁺ references indicates average Fe valence state between 0 and +2 in Pd₁Fe SAA@PC catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fe K-edge XANES spectrum showed that the edge position of Fe was located between those in reference samples, indicating that the average valence state of Fe was between 0 and +2 (Figure 2d).

nodes.characterization_summary: FT k³-weighted Fe K-edge EXAFS shows peaks at 1.44 Å (Fe-C), 1.71 Å (Fe-P), 2.23 Å (Fe-Fe).
nodes.evidence_snippet: FT k³-weighted Fe K-edge EXAFS spectra of Pd₁Fe SAA@PC implied that three characteristic peaks of Fe located at 1.44, 1.71, and 2.23 Å belonged to the scattering of Fe-C, Fe-P, and Fe-Fe coordination bonds.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pd K-edge WT-EXAFS shows peaks at 3.8 Å⁻¹ (Pd-P) and 9.0 Å⁻¹ (Pd-Fe); no Pd-Pd coordination confirms isolation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Pd K-edge WT contour plots of Pd₁Fe SAA@PC exhibited two positions with prominent peaks at 3.8 and 9.0 Å⁻¹, which corresponded to the Pd-P and Pd-Fe bonds.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe K-edge WT-EXAFS shows maximum peak at 3.8 Å⁻¹ (Fe-C) with extended k-values from Fe-Fe and Fe-P coordination.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fe K-edge WT contour plots exhibited a maximum peak at 3.8 Å⁻¹, which was attributed to the signal peaks of the Fe-C bonds.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pd first shell: CN=4 with Pd-C (2.01 Å), Pd-P (2.21 Å), Pd-Fe×2 (2.62 Å); confirms atomic dispersion and coordination.
nodes.evidence_snippet: According to the fitting results, the first shell of the central atom Pd displayed a coordination number of four, directly connected by one C atom, one P atom, and two Fe atoms, with the mean bond lengths of 2.01, 2.21, and 2.62 Å respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pd 3d peaks at 342.4 eV (Pd²⁺ 3d3/2), 341.0 eV (Pd⁰ 3d3/2), 336.7 eV (Pd²⁺ 3d5/2), 335.8 eV (Pd⁰ 3d5/2); 0.23 eV lower BE shift vs Pd₁Fe SAA@C due to P electron compensation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Pd 3d XPS fitted curves of Pd₁Fe SAA@PC manifested four peaks, which were assigned to Pd²⁺ 3d3/2 (342.4 eV), Pd⁰ 3d3/2 (341.0 eV), Pd²⁺ 3d5/2 (336.7 eV), and Pd⁰ 3d5/2 (335.8 eV)... shifted by 0.23 eV toward lower binding energies compared to that of Pd₁Fe SAA@C.

nodes.characterization_summary: P 2p XPS shows 0.49 eV higher binding energy shift vs Fe NP@PC, indicating increased P valence state upon Pd doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, the P 2p XPS spectrum revealed a higher binding energy shift of 0.49 eV for the characteristic peak of Pd₁Fe SAA@PC compared to that of Fe NP@PC.

nodes.characterization_summary: UPS shows work function increases with Pd doping and decreases with P doping in Pd₁Fe SAA@PC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ultraviolet photoelectron spectrometry analysis was conducted on different samples to demonstrate the Schottky effect... The results revealed that the overall catalyst work function (ϕ) increased with Pd doping and decreased with P doping.

nodes.characterization_summary: Geometric phase analysis of HRTEM shows ε_xx and ε_yy strain tensor components confirming lattice strain scalability from Pd modification in Fe.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Additionally, we employed geometric phase analysis to investigate the impact of atomically dispersed Pd modifications in Fe on the lattice strain. The ε_xx and ε_yy components of the strain tensor demonstrated notable scalability of the alloy (Figure S16).
